dedupe_keys.name: tomorrowville virtual urban testbed of a global south city for multi hazard risk kathmandu and nairobi contexts

description: Tomorrowville is a digital urban scenario built as a testbed for multi-hazard risk assessment and for evaluating urbanisation scenarios in a Global South setting, covering 500 hectares located south of Kathmandu, Nepal, with socio-economic properties drawn also from Nairobi, Kenya. It was published by the Environmental Information Data Centre on 22 April 2025 by researchers from the Universities of Edinburgh, Bristol, Glasgow and Leeds, University College London and Anofa, funded by NERC through the GCRF Urban Disaster Risk Hub (Tomorrow's Cities). It holds building footprints for today and 50 years ahead, modified from OpenStreetMap with a taxonomy string for code level, storeys, occupancy and structural system; land use for both times; earthquake and flood vulnerability functions; synthetic households with education, age, gender and work status; and earthquake, flood and debris-flow hazard intensities. Coverage: one synthetic 500 ha area. Access: EIDC data package and supporting information. Licence: Open Government Licence; free. Caveats: the social data are synthetic and do not reflect reality on the ground. Simulation uses: testing risk-informed urban planning, future development scenarios and multi-hazard impact tools. Related records: the Tomorrow's Cities multi-hazard future scenarios for ten cities and the Onslow testbed.
